key_insight: A matrix-free FFT solver using scaled boundary finite elements offers a softer alternative to fully integrated voxel elements while remaining stable in tested porous microstructures.
engineering_relevance: The method supports elastic homogenization of porous and highly heterogeneous materials on regular voxel grids without assembling or storing a global stiffness matrix.
method: Discretize a periodic voxel grid with hexahedral SBFEM cells and analytical radial solutions.
Apply a homogeneous SBFEM stiffness preconditioner locally in Fourier space.
Bound the preconditioned system’s condition number by material contrast, independently of grid resolution.
evidence_signal: Tests on a short-fibre composite, polyurethane foam, and sand-based binder jet microstructure showed robust convergence and competitive accuracy, including stability where reduced-integration elements became unstable.
watch_item: The condition-number bound depends on material contrast, so grid independence alone does not guarantee contrast-independent convergence.
paper_title: Scaled boundary finite elements for FFT-based computational micromechanics
